blurb: Short-legged Persian and Munchkin cross, formerly called the Napoleon
description: The Minuet, formerly the Napoleon, is an American Persian and Munchkin cross: short-legged, flat-faced, long or short coat, recognized by TICA but few others.
answer: The Minuet, originally called the Napoleon, is a hybrid cat breed developed in the United States from 1996 by crossing Persians with Munchkins. It combines the Munchkin's short legs with the Persian's shortened face and comes in long-haired and short-haired varieties; most major registries do not recognize it because of welfare concerns.

body: Joe Smith began breeding Persians with Munchkins in 1996, having previously bred Basset Hounds. The name Napoleon was chosen in reference to the belief that Napoleon Bonaparte was short. TICA added the breed to its experimental category in 2001, granted registration-only status in 2002 and preliminary status by 2011, and renamed it the Minuet in January 2015. It became eligible for full TICA championship in 2016.

TICA permits only Minuets, Munchkins and Persian-type breeds (Persians, Himalayans and Exotic Shorthairs) in breeding. The CFA, FIFe, GCCF and WCF do not recognize the breed due to welfare concerns, and breeding it is prohibited by law in Victoria, Australia.

The Minuet has the short legs of the Munchkin, caused by a dwarfism mutation, and the shortened face of the Persian. The body is semi-cobby and low to the ground, the tail is not short relative to the body, the ears are rounded and set wide apart, and the eyes are large and round. It comes in long-haired and short-haired varieties in any coat color.
The source material gives little information on the Minuet's personality. Individual cats vary, and temperament is often described in terms of the two parent breeds.

Sources give little specific care advice. Long-haired individuals will need regular grooming, and because of the breed's flat face and short limbs, close attention to breathing, eyes, teeth and joints with a veterinarian is advisable.

The Minuet can inherit problems from both its dwarfism and its flat face. Conditions reported in the breed include achondrodysplasia, with signs such as thick joints, an undersized jaw and a curved spine; a higher incidence of lordosis and pectus excavatum; and a heightened risk of osteoarthritis.

Brachycephaly-related conditions reported include breathing difficulty, brachycephalic airway obstruction syndrome, tear overflow (epiphora) with skin staining, exophthalmos, corneal sequestra, dental and periodontal disease from jaw malformation, and dystocia.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Minuet and a Napoleon cat?
faq.a: They are the same breed. TICA changed the name from Napoleon to Minuet in 2015, though some registries still use the original name.

faq.q: Why is the Minuet not recognized by most registries?
faq.a: Registries such as the CFA, FIFe, GCCF and WCF do not recognize it because of welfare concerns about health problems linked to dwarfism and a flat face.

faq.q: Do Minuet cats have health problems?
faq.a: Conditions reported in the breed include achondrodysplasia, osteoarthritis risk, spinal and chest deformities, and brachycephalic breathing, eye and dental problems.
